headline: Showers Monday, then a Tuesday night–Wednesday front brings lowland rain, first notable Cascade snow, and a cooler, drier weekend.
summary: As of Sunday evening, a weakening low off the coast is drifting south and moves onto northwest Oregon by Monday afternoon. Until then western Washington sees periodic showers, with steadier rain at times over the Cascades and coast. Highs stay in the 50s Monday, and the snow level is near 5,000 feet, so only the high mountains get snow. Winds are easing tonight along the coast and around Admiralty Inlet. Tuesday stays unsettled, with a few Cascade showers and highs in the mid 50s. A front from British Columbia arrives late Tuesday and crosses Tuesday night into Wednesday, bringing more rain, locally breezy winds, and colder air. Forecasters call it the first noticeable mountain snow event of the season. Snow levels during the heaviest precipitation are 3,500 to 4,500 feet, so higher Cascade passes could see snow, mostly Tuesday evening into early Wednesday. Lowlands get rain Wednesday, with a small 15% chance of thunderstorms in most lowland areas. Snow amounts are uncertain: the chance of more than 6 inches in the 24 hours ending 5 PM Wednesday is about 90% at Paradise and 70% at Heather Meadows (Mt. Baker), but only 20% at Stevens Pass and 15% at Rainy Pass. Forecasters haven't decided whether a winter weather alert is needed, and none has been issued. The low behind the front deepens offshore Thursday and lingers into late week, keeping things unsettled. By late Friday into the weekend, the storm track is expected to shift farther south, lowering the chance of precipitation and making temperatures cooler. Forecasters will watch for morning frost or freezing. No watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect for land areas.
changes: Earlier discussions focused on rain and breezy winds today, with the midweek system bringing about 4 inches of pass snow. By afternoon, forecasters gave site-by-site odds for Cascade snow (high at Paradise and Mt. Baker, low at Stevens and Rainy Pass), added a 15% thunderstorm chance, and added a cooler, drier weekend with possible frost or freezing.
